concepts.name: Latitude and longitude
concepts.mechanism: Latitude locates a place north or south of the Equator; longitude locates it east or west of a reference meridian. Both are angular coordinates. A coordinate pair requires direction and a reference system; latitude and longitude are not interchangeable.
concepts.example: 20 degrees north, 70 degrees east identifies a position using two different angular measurements. Two places can share latitude but differ in longitude.
concepts.mistake: Latitude is not distance east of Greenwich, and a single coordinate usually does not uniquely locate a place.
items: Two places share 20 degrees north but have different longitudes. What is shared?
Which coordinate describes east/west angular position?

concepts.name: Map scale and distance
concepts.mechanism: A representative fraction compares map distance with ground distance in the same units. At 1:50,000, one centimetre represents 50,000 centimetres or 500 metres. A larger-scale map has a smaller denominator and usually covers less area with more detail.
concepts.example: Two centimetres on a 1:50,000 map represent one kilometre on the ground. Enlarging a digital image requires updating its scale representation.
concepts.mistake: A larger scale does not mean a larger region, and centimetres must be converted before reporting kilometres.

concepts.name: Map projections and distortion
concepts.mechanism: Flattening Earth's curved surface into a map cannot preserve area, shape, distance and direction everywhere at once. Choose a projection for the task and disclose distortion. Equal-area maps are suitable for comparing area; conformal maps preserve local angles, not universal area.
concepts.example: A world map can make high-latitude regions look disproportionately large. An equal-area projection is a better starting point for area comparisons.
concepts.mistake: A familiar world map is not a distortion-free picture of the planet.
items: Can a flat world map preserve every geometric property globally?
Yes, if north is at the top
Yes, if the colours are correct
Which projection property matters for comparing countries' areas?
Only whether the map is popular
Two world maps show different apparent sizes of the same polar region. What should be investigated first?
Whether the region doubled in size overnight
Whether the map has enough labels

concepts.name: Rotation, revolution and seasons
concepts.mechanism: Rotation produces the daily illumination cycle. Seasons primarily arise from axial tilt combined with revolution, changing solar angle and day length. Opposite hemispheres receive different seasonal illumination; changing Earth-Sun distance is not the main seasonal cause.
concepts.example: When the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun, the Southern Hemisphere tilts away. A planet with little tilt can still rotate and have day/night.
concepts.mistake: Summer is not simply the whole planet moving closer to the Sun, and rotation is not revolution.
items: Earth's daily day/night cycle mainly results from—
What primarily explains opposite seasons in the two hemispheres?
Both hemispheres being closer to the Sun together
The Moon changing Earth's map scale
Imagine an otherwise similar planet with very little axial tilt. Which change is most plausible?
Weaker tilt-driven seasonal contrasts while rotation still produces day/night
Every hemisphere must have stronger seasons
The planet cannot orbit a star
